records.notes: The industry's own self-protection playbook. Defines what a shipowner is already expected to do — i.e. the baseline any escort service is sold on top of.

records.name: BMP5 — Best Management Practices to Deter Piracy and Enhance Maritime Security in the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Indian Ocean and Arabian Sea
records.publisher: BIMCO, ICS, IGP&I Clubs, INTERTANKO and OCIMF
records.notes: Superseded in March 2025 by the consolidated BMP Maritime Security, and again by Version 2 in 2026. Retained because BMP5's threat section is the most detailed public description of pirate tactics available, and the tactics have not changed.

records.name: Castor Vali SEV support across the Gulf of Guinea
The Rise of Private Maritime Security Companies
records.publisher: David Isenberg, Cato Institute (first published in Somalia Report)
records.notes: HISTORICAL. Every price in it is from 2012, at the peak of Somali piracy. Aggregates Stratfor, the Independent Maritime Security Association and SAMI. The only detailed public source found on private maritime security pricing and on convoy escort economics — re-base against a live broker quote before commercial use.

records.name: Suez Canal vs Cape Route: Comparing Cost, Time and Risk in 2026
records.notes: Industry blog aggregating carrier and analyst figures. Directionally consistent with other sources here, but one war-risk baseline it quotes (0.0001% of hull value) is implausible by three orders of magnitude against every other source in this library, so none of its insurance figures are used.

records.name: Saildrone Business Breakdown and Founding Story
Crime at Sea: A Global Database of Maritime Pirate Attacks (1993-2020)
records.publisher: Journal of Open Humanities Data / Zenodo / GitHub
records.notes: 7,511 IMB-reported attacks, tidied and augmented with geospatial data. DOI 10.5334/johd.39. Fields: date, time, lat/lon, attack type, location description, nearest country, EEZ, distance from shore, vessel name/type/status. Ends December 2020.

records.name: Non-US USV builder discovery pass, 3 September 2026

records.notes: Schema-constrained discovery of USV builders across Ukraine, Turkey, Israel, China, Korea, Japan, India, Singapore, UAE, Australia and Europe. Returned 42 entries with per-company source URLs. Platform names and contract claims come from company pages and defence trade press; not independently audited.
